documents.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: Immunotherapy is an essential treatment strategy for lung cancer, yet resistance to it is often unavoidable, resulting in treatment failure and poor prognosis. The cancer stem cell (CSC) theory offers a valuable perspective for understanding tumor metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy. However, there is a scarcity of multi-omics studies that identify tumor stemness subpopulations and their associated signaling pathways. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics sequencing (ST-seq) to identify a myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11)-high stemnes

documents.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic driver of mesenchymal plasticity and vascular microenvironment remodeling in glioblastoma.
documents.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by pronounced microenvironmental heterogeneity, severe hypoxia, and profound resistance to conventional and targeted therapies. While abnormal tumor angiogenesis and perivascular niches are recognized hallmarks of GBM, the tumor-intrinsic drivers that actively orchestrate malignant-endothelial crosstalk and structure protective vascular sanctuaries remain to be fully defined. To identify key tumor-intrinsic vascular orchestrators, this study focused on PDIA6 and investigated its functional role and clinical significance in GBM mesenchymal plasticity, maligna

documents.title: Mouse spatial transcriptomics implicates the thalamus and cortex in autism and schizophrenia.
documents.abstract: The past decade has seen tremendous progress in the identification of genes associated with complex neuropsychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia. Expression patterns of these genes in single cell data strongly implicate excitatory and inhibitory neurons; however, there are limited data on the brain regions involved - a critical question for neurobiology. Spatial transcriptomics provide an opportunity to perform systematic multi-regional analyses to provide insights into this question.

documents.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
documents.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient- and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric soli
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
documents.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
documents.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n

documents.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
documents.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. The current release con

documents.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
documents.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat

documents.title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex.
documents.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) exhibit both overlapping and distinct clinical features, including sex differences in prevalence and symptomatology, but how these similarities and differences are reflected at the molecular and cellular level in the human brain remains poorly understood. Here, we applied spatial transcriptomics to the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from individuals with MDD, BD, and neurotypical controls to resolve molecular programs associated with diagnosis and biological sex. Our analysis revealed sex- and diagnosis-specific differences across
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Overcoming segmentation bottlenecks in brain tissue for spatial proteomic inference at population scale.
documents.abstract: In spatial proteomics across large cohorts, downstream estimates from tens of thousands of images depend on accurate cell segmentation. Yet pretrained segmentation models struggle with morphologically complex cell bodies in human brain tissue, and how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery remains unclear. Here, we introduce SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference developed using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the human prefrontal cortex. After benchmarking eight segmentation methods spanning classical, convolutional, and foundati
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: spaTransfer: transfer learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data using non-negative matrix factorization.
documents.abstract: Recent advances in spatially-resolved transcriptomics have enabled profiling of gene expression in a spatial context, which has led to the generation of large-scale single-cell and spatial atlases with computationally-derived cell type or spatial domain labels. An increasingly important task with these data has become the transfer of cell type or spatial domain annotations from a given reference (or source) atlas into a new target tissue or sample. The reference and target datasets could be at different resolutions or measured on different experimental platforms. Here, we present a method to p
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.
documents.abstract: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin with sequencing (scATAC-seq) is widely used to investigate chromatin accessibility but experiments often contain empty droplets, droplets containing damaged nuclei or cellular-debris. Accurately filtering high-quality nuclei is important as noisy droplets contribute reads that can distort downstream analysis and obscure rare cell population. Current approaches often rely on read depth and or predefined genomic features that are not exactly the same as chromatin accessibility landscape. Here, we present a Shannon entropy-based method that f
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: CellWHISPER disentangles direct cell-cell communication from structural proximity.
documents.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics makes it possible to infer direct, contact-dependent cellular communication, but existing tools are prone to high error rates due to spatial structure in cell types and gene expression. We present CellWHISPER, a framework for inferring contact-mediated communication, including gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling, from spatial transcriptomics data. CellWHISPER controls errors with a statistical procedure that accounts for confounding effects of cell-type-specific expression and spatial organization. Closed-form significance scores enable analysis of large data. A
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer.
documents.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables region-resolved investigation of tumor metabolism, yet translating gene expression into reliable metabolic flux predictions remains challenging because genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs). Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomic data from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor, spanning normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3 and 3+4 tissues, with Human-GEM using an E-Flux framework incorporating defined nutrient constraints, explicit cycle certification, and loopless flux variability analysis. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement.
documents.abstract: Targeted spatial transcriptomics platforms such as 10x Genomics Xenium measure a predefined panel of genes. A gene is usually detected in fewer cells in the spatial assay than in the single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) reference used to choose it, by an amount that differs from gene to gene. We present eXtensible Spatial Panel Evaluation And Refinement (X- SPEAR), a framework for designing and checking Xenium gene panels. Its marker-selection method, Decision-rule Aggregation for Rare-cell Typing (DART), learns short Boolean gene rules and keeps several gene-disjoint rules per cell type. DA
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Survival-associated cellular communication networks in human solid cancers.
documents.abstract: Single-cell atlases have enabled the prediction of human cell-cell communication (CCC) networks in cancer, but whether predicted communication networks have clinical significance is not well understood. Here, we integrated a pan-solid cancer scRNA-seq atlas comprising 78 cell types from 318,426 quality-controlled cells with bulk RNA-seq and clinical outcome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) to develop Single-cell-based Kaplan-Meier Analysis Network (SKyNet). SKyNet prioritizes ligand-receptor interactions associated with overall survival across 11 human solid cancers, predicting unique
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Dose-additive and dose-dependent fetal testis toxicity of a nine-phthalate mixture in the rat.
documents.abstract: Phthalates (ortho-phthalic acid diesters) are used in a variety of manufacturing processes, particularly as non-covalent plasticizers in flexible polyvinyl chloride. Phthalates are male reproductive toxicants that disrupt the development of the fetal testis, resulting in malformed seminiferous cords, multinucleated germ cells (MNGs), and decreased testosterone production. We previously reported that MNGs were a sensitive, dose-dependent marker of dipentyl phthalate (DPEP) germ cell toxicity. To test whether germ cell effects of phthalates are dose-additive, we measured the induction of MNGs by
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
documents.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised

documents.title: SVC: A Vision Transformer-based Spatially and Virtually Embedded Cell Model for Deciphering Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomic Heterogeneity.
documents.abstract: Subcellular transcript localization shapes gene regulation and cellular function, yet profiling it at scale remains difficult, limiting our ability to study subcellular heterogeneity across tissues and disease. Here, we present SVC, a Vision Transformer-based spatially and virtually embedded cell model that learns subcellular transcript organization within native tissue context directly from subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics. SVC represents each gene's subcellular localization as an image patch and uses other genes within the same cell as context, enabling subcellular contextual l
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. documents.title: ALBIS: simulation of multi-resolution and multi-dimensional spatial transcriptomics data.
documents.abstract: The rapid adoption of spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies has been accompanied by substantial growth in computational methods, creating an increasing need for systematic and reliable benchmarking, particularly as analyses increasingly extend from individual tissue sections to three-dimensional (3D) tissue reconstruction. Existing benchmarks often rely on a small and similar set of experimentally-derived datasets because they offer a reliable ground truth label, which is hard to find in practice. Simulated or synthetic data provide an alternative, yet most existing simulators either adapt
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Deep-learning-driven tumor microenvironment profiling improves immunotherapy response prediction.
documents.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the management of many cancers, such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet durable clinical benefit is achieved in only a subset of patients. Immunotherapy outcomes are governed by the multicellular tumor microenvironment (TME), through the structured and directional interplay of regulatory programs and ligand-receptor communications. Yet most existing methods for immunotherapy response prediction rely on independent signatures or cell types and fail to model the structured and directional signaling network within the TME. To address this gap, we introdu
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Spatially resolved tumor-microenvironment architecture defines therapeutic response in unresectable hepatoblastoma.
documents.abstract: Hepatoblastoma exhibits variable therapeutic response that is not fully explained by current risk stratification. While prior studies have characterized tumor composition, the role of spatial organization in determining outcome, particularly in unresectable disease requiring transplantation under immunosuppression, remains unclear.
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: An integrated multi-omic atlas of the choroid plexus highlights conserved molecular programs of epithelial function.
documents.abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a specialized epithelial tissue responsible for production of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), maintenance of the blood-CSF barrier and regulation of CSF-borne signaling factors. However, despite the ChP's central role in CSF homeostasis, conserved molecular programs of ChP epithelial function across species and conditions remain incompletely defined. In this study, we integrated eight mouse and human single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq datasets to build a multi-species ChP atlas capturing major epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune populations. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
documents.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se

documents.title: Detection of Supporting-Cell-Associated Gene Transcripts in Adult Human Cochlear Tissue from Cadaveric Temporal Bones.
documents.abstract: The adult human cochlea is difficult to study because viable inner-ear tissue is rarely available and postmortem samples are technically challenging to process. Supporting cells are essential for cochlear architecture, ionic and osmotic balance, synaptic stability, stress responses, and potential regenerative signaling. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of detecting transcripts associated with cochlear supporting-cell biology in adult human cadaveric cochlear tissue.

documents.title: PathwayFinder enables linked exploration of cell types and gene modules in spatially resolved transcriptomics data.
documents.abstract: The rapid development of spatially resolved transcriptomics technologies has provided opportunities and challenges for understanding biological systems. Interpreting these data requires integrated analysis of gene expression and cell types within their spatial context, however, existing tools fall short in scaling this linked interactive exploration to large-scale datasets. We present PathwayFinder, a visual analytics application designed to bridge the gap between gene-centric and cell-centric analysis. Unlike standard workflows that view cells and genes in isolation, PathwayFinder links them

documents.title: The CD39/CD73 adenosinergic pathway is increased by proinflammatory states and modified by chemo-radiation in human non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: Recent clinical trials show prominent anti-tumor activity of CD73-blocking antibodies in combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) antagonists in a subset of patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which highlights the need to understand the properties of the CD39/CD73 pathway in human lung malignancies and its modulation by other anti-cancer therapies. To address this, we study the distribution, biological context, spatial heterogeneity, clinical significance, and modulation of CD39/CD73 using multiplexed quantitative immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomic

documents.title: Dupilumab modulates type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis.
documents.abstract: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (eCRS) is a refractory type 2 inflammatory disease characterized by nasal polyp formation and eosinophilic infiltration. Although dupilumab, an IL-4Rα-blocking antibody, demonstrates clinical efficacy, its cellular mechanisms within nasal polyps remain unclear.
documents.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

documents.title: BGN marks cancer-associated fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix remodeling in HNSCC.
documents.abstract: Biglycan (BGN) is an important component of the extracellular matrix (ECM). Using an integrated analysis of TCGA bulk RNA-sequencing, single-cell RNA-sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic datasets, we systematically characterized the expression patterns, prognostic significance, and biological roles of BGN in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and survival analyses in independent clinical cohorts further validated the expression pattern, abundance, and prognostic significance of BGN. The biological role of BGN was further investigated using

documents.title: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort.
documents.abstract: Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk.

documents.title: Response to comments on "SpatialDG: a novel spatial domain identification method for spatially resolved transcriptomics data based on dual-graph neural network".
documents.abstract: We respond to concerns regarding reference-label-informed epoch selection in SpatialDG. We acknowledge this limitation and report a matched DLPFC reevaluation of SpatialDG and Spatial-MGCN under the same reference-label-independent checkpoint-selection rule, in which SpatialDG achieved the higher three-seed mean ARI on all 12 slices.

documents.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. documents.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d

documents.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
documents.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod

documents.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
documents.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

documents.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
documents.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.

documents.title: Contrasting Spatial Genomic Structure in Two Widespread Grassland Species Across Norway Supports Species-Specific Seed Sourcing.
documents.abstract: Ecological restoration typically relies on locally sourced seed material, yet seed sourcing in many countries is based on broad administrative regions rather than empirical genetic data. Whether these generalized zones reflect biologically meaningful population genomic structure, particularly among co-occurring species used together in restoration, remains poorly understood, thus limiting genetically informed restoration practices. documents.title: An ibuprofen-eluting electrospun membrane prevents ureteral fibrosis by dampening macrophage-associated fibroblast activation.
documents.abstract: Ureteral stricture is driven by unresolved inflammation and progressive matrix deposition, yet mechanism-guided local therapies remain limited.

documents.title: Reanalysis of public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomes identifies widespread tumor-normal dysregulation and a cross-layer cell-cycle signal in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.
documents.abstract: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) is a rare malignancy affecting the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection identified as a critical etiological factor in a subset of cases. HPV-positive and HPV-negative SNSCC exhibit distinct clinical behaviors, with HPV-positive tumors generally demonstrating better prognosis and treatment response. However, the cellular composition and transcriptomic landscape of SNSCC tumor versus normal tissue remain incompletely characterized. Multi-layer transcriptomic reanalysis of publicly available single-nucleus and bul

documents.title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
documents.abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks. documents.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
documents.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH.

documents.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
documents.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα (PPP2R1A), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood.

documents.title: Immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor axes in osteoarthritis: microenvironmental control of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate.
documents.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is increasingly recognized as a whole-joint disease shaped by chronic low-grade inflammation, matrix damage, mechanical stress, and failed tissue repair. Beyond the traditional view of cartilage wear, emerging evidence indicates that immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor (LR) communication plays a central role in translating microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. In this narrative review, we summarize major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified LR axes that regulate OA progression, including cytokine pathways such as IL-1β-IL-1R, TNF-α-TNFR, I

documents.title: A curvilinear coordinate flatmap for visualizing hippocampal structure and development.
documents.abstract: The hippocampal formation is a highly curved and topographically complex forebrain structure. This complex geometry presents persistent challenges for analyzing subregional, laminar, and connectivity patterns. Here, we present a computational workflow that generates curvilinear-coordinate flatmaps from mouse Common Coordinate Framework (CCF) registered hippocampal and retrohippocampal regions by solving the Laplacian equation to derive geodesic streamlines. documents.title: A Spatial Multiomics Atlas and Resource for Immune-Fibrotic Niches in Chronic Kidney Allograft Dysfunction.
documents.abstract: Chronic allograft dysfunction (CAD) is a major cause of late kidney-allograft failure, yet its spatially organized cellular and metabolic mechanisms remain poorly resolved because human biopsies are scarce and experimental models are imperfect. Here, we established a tacrolimus-modulated accelerated mouse model of CAD and constructed a cross-species multiomics atlas by integrating mouse single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex imaging with human single-nucleus RNA sequencing, Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics.
